subject: Culture
title: Mediterranean Honor Codes
description: A quick win: understand Mediterranean Honor Codes.

hook.text: In 1800s Sicily a man who didn't avenge an insult was called 'cornuto' and barred from village life.

buildup.text: Anthropologist Julian Pitt-Rivers mapped the honor belt from Spain through Greece to North Africa.

discovery.text: In these regions honor belonged to the family, not the individual. One person's shame stained everyone.

twist.text: State courts couldn't replace honor codes because courts were slow and corrupt. Honor was instant justice.

climax.text: Even today, parts of southern Italy have lower crime not from police but from community shame pressure.

punchline.text: Honor codes thrive where institutions fail.

quiz.question: Who mapped the Mediterranean honor belt?

details.summary: Mediterranean honor codes shaped societies from ancient Greece to modern Sicily, centering on masculine reputation, female sexual purity, and the obligation to avenge insults.
details.whyItMatters: Mediterranean honor codes explain the cultural logic behind the Mafia, vendetta traditions, and why certain Mediterranean societies developed specific attitudes toward gender, violence, and silence.
takeaways: Mediterranean honor tied male status to female family members' purity
Omertà (code of silence) protected Mafia honor above the law
Greek philotimo combines honor, pride, and social obligation

faq.question: What is omertà and where does it originate?
faq.answer: Omertà is the Mafia code of silence — never cooperate with authorities or betray family secrets. It originated in Southern Italian honor culture where resolving disputes internally demonstrated strength and self-sufficiency.

faq.question: What is Greek philotimo?
faq.answer: Philotimo literally means 'love of honor' — it combines personal dignity, social obligation, generosity, and doing the right thing even at personal cost. Greeks consider it untranslatable and central to their identity.
